svg.aria-label: How to write જ ો ં ી ુ છ ક ણ શ: 9 parts, જ, ો, ં, ી, ુ, છ, ક, ણ, શ, one after another
svg.title: Writing જ ો ં ી ુ છ ક ણ શ
svg.desc: 9 parts written one after another: જ, ો, ં, ી, ુ, છ, ક, ણ, શ (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: જ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, જ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ો: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/8_ko.svg, groups g1 then g2 (strokes g1s0, g2s0): the o sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ં: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/10_kam.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the anusvara drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ી: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/3_kee.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the ii sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ુ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/4_ku.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the u sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; છ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, છ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ક: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ક animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ણ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ણ animation, first through third SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; શ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, શ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: જ: The teaching app animates જ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins near the upper left, circles the upper-left loop, continues diagonally down-right through the crossing body, circles the lower-right loop, then rises diagonally into the long upper-right exit without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the left loop, diagonal crossing, right loop, and long upper-right exit, but its printed loops are broader and its crossing more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's left-loop-to-crossing-to-right-loop-to-exit order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loops, crossing, and exit differently. ો: In the template for કો, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ો is two pen-down runs: the ા bar first, from the top down into its foot, then the flag above it, from its upper-left tip down to the right. t30apps, already cited for ઓ, draws its trailing stem before its high arc. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: its most common form of the o sign (42 of 83 prototypes, 51%) is two strokes, the bar first. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ં: In the template for કં, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ં is one pen-down run: a small closed loop that starts at its top and turns anticlockwise. The printed dot is solid, so the pen path circles inside it. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 156 of its 157 stored prototypes of the anusvara are one stroke, 72% of them anticlockwise. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ી: In the template for કી, and in all 34 consonant rows, ી is one pen-down run that starts at the left tip of the top hook, arches up and over to the right, comes down the right stem and ends in a foot to the right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: its one-stroke prototypes of the ii sign (32 of 91, 35%) also start on the left and end at the lower right, though its most common form (51 of 91) is two strokes. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ુ: In the template for કુ, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ુ is one pen-down run that starts directly below the consonant, at the top of the sign, swings right and down round the bowl, and ends at its upper left. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 79 of its 83 stored prototypes of the u sign (95%) are one stroke, and 82% of those turn clockwise. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. છ: The teaching app animates છ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins near the upper left, circles clockwise around the upper-left lobe, turns back through the middle, continues clockwise around the broad lower body, climbs the tall outer-right curve, then circles the upper-right lobe and finishes beside the outer curve without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves both upper lobes, the middle turn, broad lower body, and tall outer-right curve, but its printed bodies are broader and the right lobe more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-left-lobe-to-lower-body-to-upper-right-lobe order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the lobes, body, curve, and terminals differently. ક: The teaching app animates ક as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles left around the upper loop, continues diagonally down-right through the middle crossing, then circles the rounded lower body and finishes at the lower left. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path sweeps a separate diagonal cross-stroke from lower left to upper right. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the upper loop, central diagonal, rounded lower body, and crossing diagonal, but its printed loops are broader and the crossing more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's joined-loop-body-before-diagonal-cross-stroke order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loops, diagonal, and terminals differently. ણ: The teaching app animates ણ as three ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path descends the left spine, then sweeps through the hooked lower tail. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path circles the separate rounded middle bowl. It lifts again and its third SVG path descends the tall right spine before turning through the lower foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the hooked body, middle bowl, and tall right spine, but its printed body is broader, its tail descends below the baseline, and its joins and foot are more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-middle-bowl-before-right-spine order and two-lift evidence while fitting all three runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, join, or slant the body, hook, bowl, spine, and terminals differently. શ: The teaching app animates શ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper right, circles the small upper loop, then continues through the broad lower body and into its lower-right tail. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper loop, broad lower body, tail, tall spine, and lower foot, but its printed body is wider and more angular and its spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-body-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, body, tail, spine, foot, and terminals differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 9 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 9 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 2 of 9 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Part 3 of 9 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 4 of 9 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
